trust_decision.summary: An embedded file name read from an untrusted PRX/STX container is joined to a temp dir and written there, with no check that the result stays inside that dir (the zip expander already checks this).

landing_point.why: The summary names the P3 PRX and SureTrak STX readers, and extractFile is where the embedded name becomes a File.

fix_sites.entry_point: public API P3PRXFileReader.read(InputStream/File/String), and UniversalProjectReader.read via the DOS-EXE PRX fingerprint (src/main/java/org/mpxj/reader/UniversalProjectReader.java:949)
public API SureTrakSTXFileReader.read, and UniversalProjectReader.read via the STX fingerprint (src/main/java/org/mpxj/reader/UniversalProjectReader.java:962)
fix_sites.module_kind: format reader in a different package (sibling implementation)

fix_sites.entry_point: new helper FileHelper.validateTargetFileIsInParentDirectory, not an entry point
UniversalProjectReader zip handling (src/main/java/org/mpxj/reader/UniversalProjectReader.java:711); refactor only, same check moved into the helper

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The STX reader (src/main/java/org/mpxj/primavera/suretrak/SureTrakSTXFileReader.java:90) is a second copy of the same extractFile logic in another package, but the advisory summary names it, so it is not out of scope. The InputStreamHelper change is a refactor only.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver who reads only the PRX path could argue STX is a separate format. The summary names both, so this argument is weak.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate PRX/STX containers carry DOS 8.3 file names with dots and extensions (P3/SureTrak database files), and the readers must still extract them into tempDir and read them back. An over-broad fix (rejecting any dot, or allowing only alphanumerics) breaks PRX/STX reading. The zip expander must also keep creating nested subdirectories.

O6_input_shapes: relative '..' segments in the 13-byte PRX name field (src/main/java/org/mpxj/primavera/p3/P3PRXFileReader.java:97)
relative '..' segments in the 260-byte STX name field (src/main/java/org/mpxj/primavera/suretrak/SureTrakSTXFileReader.java:85)
both write branches: the zero-length createNewFile branch and the Blast-decompressed newOutputStream branch (src/main/java/org/mpxj/primavera/p3/P3PRXFileReader.java:104-115)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second archive expander (for example a tar or CAB-style container used by another legacy Primavera/Asta format) that joins entry names without calling the helper
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The project already has three hand-written expand-to-tempdir loops, each written per format. A fourth written for a new legacy format is plausible.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a name decoder that maps a byte such as '\\' to '/' or trims after the check, giving a parser differential on the embedded name
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: DOS/Windows-origin formats store backslash paths, so a maintainer normalising separators after validation is realistic (a how-type sibling).

O9_family: path traversal / zip-slip style archive extraction (CWE-22)

O10_build.project_tests: No PRX/STX-specific tests found under src/test (glob returned nothing); the fix adds no tests.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Copy the zip-slip canonical-path check from InputStreamHelper into P3PRXFileReader.extractFile only, and miss the identical STX copy.

out_of_scope_notes: OpcReader.exportProject and WebServicesReader write to caller-supplied paths (src/main/java/org/mpxj/opc/OpcReader.java:189, src/main/java/org/mpxj/primavera/webservices/WebServicesReader.java:129). These are not archive-controlled names, so they are not this protection.

ExternalProjectContainer resolves subproject file names from project data for reading (src/main/java/org/mpxj/ExternalProjectContainer.java:125). This is a read, not an extraction write, and was not pursued.
Blast decompression size is unbounded. This is resource exhaustion and was not pursued.
unverified: Whether a PRX/STX inside a zip reaches these readers through the recursive directory handling of UniversalProjectReader was not traced.
Advisory write-up coverage (recall risk) judged from the changelog only.
